summary: Dore Lake tower: listed at 24.4 m (80 ft) of heavy steel; a towermen list places Tom McBride there 1949 to mid-1960s and Henry Myers 1991-2001. No current-site source found.

events.note: Photo caption on the jkcc.com Dore Lake footnotes page (Memories of Dore Lake) names a Dore Tower Cabin; the only book credit on that page is Timber Trails (a Big River history), not a Dore Lake book
Tom McBride listed as towerman at Dore Lake, 1949 to mid-1960s, on a Saskatchewan towermen list
Henry Myers listed as towerman at Dore Lake, 1991-2001, on the same list
Latest date given for a Dore Lake towerman on the list (Henry Myers, 1991-2001)

Listing gives the legal land location
Listing gives the Dore Lake site coordinates

sources.title: Dore Lake Footnotes - Part Two. Memories of Dore Lake

notes_for_editor: Height 80 ft (24.4 m) on the listing matches the brief's height_m. Staffing dates come from a fan-compiled towermen list whose layout runs name, years, tower; only Tom McBride (1949 to mid-1960s) and Henry Myers (1991-2001) are read as Dore Lake entries with dates. Barry McLelland, Gene Johnson (one of three towers) and Marvin McKay also appear beside Dore Lake without dates and are left out of the story; Hilda Switzer Lundgren's seven towers do not include Dore. The 1946 caption is the only pre-1949 evidence and does not say the cabin was a lookout building. Dore River vs Dore Lake is unresolved: the index lists both, and the listing has no separate Dore River entry. The brief's events list is empty and no construction year was found. Agency and current status were not confirmed by any source read.
